canonical_claim: If the hidden transaction is a removal, GC can delete blobs that the recovered writer view still references, producing a dangling committed manifest; if it is an addition, GC over-protects blobs; without a covering snapshot, recovery can repeatedly fail with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

Plain GET absence cannot safely authorize writer-epoch re-minting because it flattens transport or access failures into not-found; lifecycle decisions must use the authoritative probe outcome. Additionally, Same uuid plus same epoch plus an unfenced body does not prove the body came from the current writer, because a vanished epoch object can let a second same-uuid process re-mint the same pair. Additionally, If both epoch and mount control objects are wiped under a live mount, a same-pair twin can still exist briefly; the residual design relies on the surviving writer fencing on its next beat rather than allowing silently persistent dual writers.

The ref lane can lose a durable transaction from its in-memory view and then permanently hide that transaction behind a snapshot, making the defect data-loss class.; When `tryPublishSnapshotAndAdvanceCheckpointOnce` encounters a `NeedsRecovery` lane, it recovers the durable gap before proceeding; recovery may issue its own `_ckpt` CAS, and a snapshot must never be published from the unrecovered cache. Additionally, For a `NeedsRecovery` publish attempt, recovery's checkpoint catch-up CAS must precede every snapshot-body PUT and the publisher's own checkpoint-advance CAS; the resulting published snapshot reflects the recovered frontier. Additionally, Snapshot adoption occurs only after both the snapshot body PUT and checkpoint advancement are durable; if checkpoint advancement conflicts, in-memory adoption does not occur during that failed retry unit. Additionally, After re-recovery from `NeedsRecovery`, the ref lane is `Ready`, `recoveryInstallCountForTest` has advanced, the published snapshot ID equals the durable removal transaction missing from the stale cache, and `resolveRef` for that removed ref returns absent.

A residual post-commit exception window remains around `eraseView` and `ContentAddressedTransaction::publishStaging`'s `out_slot`: fallible work can occur after a durable commit is made but before the commit is recorded in the caller's slot.

Two current catalog rows sharing a `life_id` are `CORRUPTED_DATA`, not a first-row-wins condition; catalog mutation, REBUILD, decommission, fold adoption, and destructive GC fail closed on that cut.; A reverse catalog index maps every catalog state to `life_id -> NamespaceLifeId{name, incarnation}`; a duplicate current `life_id` is `CORRUPTED_DATA`, makes both rows unresolvable, and causes catalog mutations, REBUILD, decommission, fold adoption, and destructive GC to fail closed.

Before the authoritative flip, an empty catalog can make `result.frontier_complete = universe_authoritative && result.frontier_proven == result.frontier_namespaces` evaluate as `0 == 0`, falsely clearing destructive suppression; an empty universe must not count as a complete frontier. Additionally, `CaGcDestructiveGateCore.tla` pins `UniverseAuthoritative == TRUE` without a sabotage, so the authoritative-universe term of the production `frontier_complete` gate is not load-bearing in the model and is false in production today.

`_ckpt.life_epoch` can receive legitimate contributions from both `CasRefCatalog::completeCreation` and the first `NamespaceBirth` chunk, and treating every different present value as corruption would wedge resumed creation and restart-before-first-write sequences.

A current catalog life can have an empty key space while a dead incarnation of the same logical namespace has objects; filtering dead keys and walking the current life can then falsely prove the frontier complete and enable destruction. Additionally, If the catalog names namespace `N` at life `Y` while `N`'s objects and shard-0 fold cursor belong to life `X`, the frontier walk can prove a complete frontier without probing `X` and destructive GC can delete live blobs from `X`.

If the catalog is absent, a sentinel fallback such as `stageATransition(ns)` can make real-incarnation namespaces look empty and let a damaged catalog produce a complete frontier; an un-cataloged namespace must be unproven rather than walked at a fabricated key.

`ReplicatedMergeTreePartCheckThread` can treat a CA disk's transient `INVALID_STATE` caused by a missing mount lease as a broken part because `isRetryableException` in `checkDataPart.cpp:70` does not list `INVALID_STATE`; the current remediation detaches the part, removes it from ZooKeeper, and queues a fetch.

Exactly two CA transient throw sites can cause destructive misclassification: `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage.cpp:1111` (`TransientNotLive`) and `:1163` (probe `Indeterminate`), both on the READ plane.

`isTransientRecoveryError` at `CasRefLedger.cpp:89-97` is a CA-internal denylist-shaped classifier with an unsafe default; it guards ref-recovery re-drive at `:1085` but is not reachable from the lifecycle-gate throw because recovery reads bypass `ref_request_controller`.

`CasFsck.cpp` resolves `life` for `walkRefStream` but omits it when calling `crossEpochFromSeal`, so a namespace drop-and-recreate during the walk can make fsck report a false unconsumed-closing-seal verdict.

`runFsckImpl` obtains its namespace universe from `Pool::listNamespaces`, which is only a union of backend `LIST` results, so a live catalog namespace omitted from `roots/` and `cas/refs/` listings is never checked and fsck can report clean.

After `_cleanup` and the cleanup item are gone, legal removal debris and fabricated catalog-entry loss can be byte-identical, so an anomaly classifier cannot accept one and reject the other without another durable evidence object. Additionally, After `_cleanup` is removed, a legal removal and fabricated entry loss can both appear as an absent catalog entry with surviving canonical life-qualified debris, so the two cases cannot be separately classified from store contents alone.
`CasRefCatalog::read` currently treats an absent catalog as a virgin empty catalog, so a permanent `Retired`-only design would allow catalog loss after `_ckpt` deletion to reopen a name for birth.

The B90 `ThreadGroup` fix makes a borrowed child retain a `shared_ptr` to its parent group so background work cannot use freed parent counters. Additionally, A borrowed `ThreadGroup` can outlive its parent counters when asynchronous or background work retains the query thread group after the query ends, causing use-after-free in parent counters or memory-tracking corruption. Additionally, A child `ThreadGroup` must retain a `parent_thread_group` `shared_ptr` so the parent remains alive while child trackers point to it through raw pointers.

The B37 `MergeTreeDeduplicationLog` fix throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` when `current_writer` is absent instead of relying on a release-build `chassert` no-op; a missing `logs_dir` remains normal for storages that do not materialize empty directories. Additionally, `MergeTreeDeduplicationLog::addPart` and `dropPart` could dereference a null `current_writer` in a release build because they relied only on `chassert`. Additionally, `MergeTreeDeduplicationLog::addPart` and `dropPart` must replace the release-no-op `chassert` with a fail-closed `LOGICAL_ERROR` when `current_writer` is null.
Safety-critical CAS decoders accept incomplete or duplicate records and unbound fold generations, so a misplaced seal can authorize skipped references.

A truncated blob can be admitted as a dedup hit because `PartWriteTxn::observeAndAdmit` checks only `hr.size >= blob_header_len` and does not compare the payload size with the caller's expected `source.size`.

A skipped live manifest `+1` can cause exact-token deletion of a blob still referenced by that manifest after another owner's `-1` folds, because exact-token deletion protects against replacement but not an owner edge absent from GC state.

The orphan-manifest sweep's premise that an unowned manifest has no folded edges is false after a precommit `+1` folds, leaving stranded in-degree edges with no possible `-1` after the manifest is deleted.

Applying a successor observation through an old resolver handle violates `NoOldHandleRetarget`; the observation must be attributed to the runtime in the current slot, not to the stale resolver runtime.

A sealer must merge `_ckpt` by semantic maximum rather than write back a stale sampled body, because stale write-back can regress the base to 0 and make the next mount report an empty namespace over live data.

B207 was fixed by re-resolving referencing refs in `runFsck` when the initial HEAD is absent; only a current ref over an absent object is classified as dangling.; The fsck phantom-dangling fix re-resolves every referencing ref at both HEAD-absent branches; a missing blob is `dangling` only if a current ref still names it, not when the ref was legitimately re-published or dropped after the initial walk.

With the cleanup budget temporarily forced from 5000 to 2, `ManifestCleanupDrainsEntireRoundWithNoSkips` reproduced the leak class by deleting 2 of 5 manifest bodies and leaving 3 survivors; the test passed after the cap was removed.; The replacement test `ManifestCleanupDrainsEntireRoundWithNoSkips` asserts that a five-manifest owner removal deletes all five manifest bodies in the same GC round.

resolveWedgeOnce must recheck the exact stored admission generation, transaction or operation identity, and bytes under state_mutex after I/O before adoption, acknowledgement, or unwedge; Before a wedge retry acts on I/O results, it re-acquires the install lock, verifies the exact stored generation/transaction identity/bytes, and reruns `checkFenceOrThrow`; stale results perform no acknowledge, unwedge, or install.; resolveWedgeOnce must preserve and compare exact generation, transaction or operation identity, and bytes after I/O under the install lock

PartManifest.payload_digest is persisted but is not generally validated by Store::readManifest, so it is not currently a complete integrity guarantee; `payload_digest` is CityHash128 over the canonical text body with the digest rendered as zero hex during hashing, and decoding recomputes and verifies it.

B1 and B2 are undefined for repaired and certified-void records when logs_applied counts only fully folded listed logs and repair paths bypass TxnApplyLedger::open; B1 accounting must be cut-scoped to records in (parent_cursor, final_cursor]; speculative repaired bodies and void observations above the final cut are separate metrics
